sections.h2: Who bills property tax for a home in Tallahassee, Florida?
sections.html:
Leon County offices bill and value Tallahassee homes, and the city is one of several bodies that levy tax on the same bill. The Leon County Property Appraiser sets value and grants exemptions, the Leon County Tax Collector prints and mails the notices, and the City of Tallahassee, the county commission and other levying bodies set the millage rates. A Tallahassee bill therefore combines city and county lines.

The tax collector explains that the appraiser builds the tax roll from values and millage, then certifies it to the collector, who mails the notices. Name or address changes go through the appraiser, not the collector. If a mortgage company pays your tax through escrow, the lender should request the original notice, and you receive a copy.

sections.h2: What is the City of Tallahassee millage rate?
sections.html:
The City of Tallahassee's own budget document says its adopted millage for fiscal year 2026 is 4.4072 mills, and state law allows cities to go up to 10.0 mills. One mill is a dollar of tax per thousand dollars of taxable value, and the city notes that the taxable value on your property appraiser record is the number the rate is applied to. That figure leaves out the county, school board and other lines on your bill.

Tallahassee's tax base is unusual. The city's budget says over half of the real property inside city limits is owned by federal, state and local governments and pays no property tax, because the city is the state capital and hosts two major universities, a community college and a vocational college. To cover fire protection on those parcels, the city charges a non-ad valorem fire assessment, which most ratepayers pay on their utility bills.

  • Residential fire assessments are charged per dwelling unit.
  • Non-residential parcels pay by square footage tier.
  • The city also collects a public service tax on electricity sales at 10% of gross sales, excluding the fuel adjustment charge.

The city holds two budget public hearings in September each year, and the Leon County Property Appraiser sends a preliminary estimate of city value in June and a final one in July, certified on July 1. Check the city or the appraiser's final millage sheet before relying on any figure.

sections.h2: When are Tallahassee property taxes due?
sections.html:
Leon County tax notices go out beginning November 1, and the tax is due before April 1 of the following year. The collector's page says delinquency starts April 1, when a delinquency fee, an advertising fee and 1.5 percent interest per month are added, along with the statutory collection costs. Within 45 days after delinquency the collector must advertise a list of delinquent taxpayers in a local newspaper.

The discount for paying early follows the statewide schedule printed on the Leon County Tax Collector's page.

The August TRIM notice shows proposed taxes before bills exist. In the city's own account, the August mailing also carries an estimate from the city's budget, followed by two public hearings in September.

sections.h2: How much is the homestead exemption in Tallahassee?
sections.html:
For the 2026 tax year, the Leon County Property Appraiser says a homestead exemption is worth up to $51,411 of value. The first $25,000 applies to all taxes, including school taxes. The remaining amount, up to $26,411, applies to assessed value over $50,000 and only to non-school taxes. Voters approved Amendment 5 in 2024, which ties that second layer to the Consumer Price Index each year.

You must own and live in the home as your permanent residence on January 1, and file by March 1. The appraiser also warns that the exemption is not automatic. The appraiser's office puts the typical savings at roughly $800 a year.

  • After the first qualifying year, the Save Our Homes cap limits annual growth in assessed value to the lower of 3% or the CPI change.
  • A sale or other change of ownership resets the property to just value the next January 1.
  • A homesteader who moves can transfer part of the accumulated savings through portability within three years, using Form DR-501T.

sections.h2: What does a Tallahassee seller owe in permits and city charges?
sections.html:
The deed tax in Florida is a state documentary stamp tax collected by the clerk, so the city-level items a seller meets are permits and utility balances. The city's budget says building permits are required for new construction, additions, alterations or repairs with labor and materials above $1,000, for both residential and commercial owners.

That matters if you did work on the house and a buyer's inspector finds it. Check permit history before you list, and ask the city's building permit staff how to close an open permit. City utility accounts for electric, gas, water, sewer, stormwater and solid waste are billed by the city, so request final readings at closing.

  • Solid waste for homes of up to six units is once-a-week curbside pickup with a 96-gallon garbage container and 64-gallon recycling container.
  • Stormwater fees are billed per equivalent residential unit.
  • Fire assessments appear on the utility bill, not the tax bill, for most city customers.

sections.h2: How do taxes work when you sell a house in Tallahassee?
sections.html:
The closing agent prorates the current year's tax and pays off any unpaid prior years from your proceeds. Ask the Leon County Tax Collector for a payoff on any year that is delinquent, since interest accrues monthly after April 1. Tax certificates are sold on unpaid accounts by June 1, and Florida law lets a certificate holder apply for a tax deed after two years.

Florida's documentary stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and every party to the document is liable for it by statute. The clerk collects it when the deed is recorded. Tallahassee parcels that carry a homestead exemption can also see a higher bill for the buyer, because the next January 1 assessment resets to market value after a sale.

sections.h2: What are the options for selling a Tallahassee house with tax due?
sections.html:
You can list it, sell to a cash buyer, or pay the tax first. Whatever you choose, the lien for unpaid tax follows the parcel and must be cleared at closing. If the property is a rental or inherited home with several unpaid years, get a payoff letter before comparing offers so the net figure is accurate.

For a rental or inherited home, also confirm who has the utility accounts and whether any city charges are past due, since final readings and unpaid balances come up at closing. Ask the Leon County Tax Collector for the exact amount, including any interest and fees, before you decide how much to net.

A cash buyer purchasing as is can close without showings or repairs, which suits owners who are behind on tax and want to settle the balance from the sale. Compare each offer against what a listing would leave after commission and repairs.

faqs.q: What is Tallahassee's property tax rate?
faqs.a: The City of Tallahassee's budget document lists an adopted millage of 4.4072 mills for fiscal year 2026. Your full bill also includes county, school and other levies, so read the Leon County bill for the total.

faqs.q: When are Leon County property taxes due in Tallahassee?
faqs.a: Taxes are due before April 1, and bills go out beginning November 1. After April 1, a delinquency fee, advertising fee and 1.5 percent monthly interest are added.

faqs.q: What is the early payment discount in Tallahassee?
faqs.a: Paying in November earns 4%, December 3%, January 2% and February 1%, according to the Leon County Tax Collector.

faqs.q: What is the homestead exemption in Tallahassee for 2026?
faqs.a: It is up to $51,411 for the 2026 tax year, per the Leon County Property Appraiser, with a March 1 filing deadline. The first $25,000 covers all taxes and the rest covers non-school taxes on value above $50,000.

faqs.q: Does Tallahassee have a lot of tax-exempt property?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's budget says over half of the real property inside city limits is owned by government entities and exempt from property tax. The city uses a fire assessment and utility transfers to cover services to those parcels.
